title: how a standalone generated viewer page gets a back-link when embedded on the website
summary: coldstart graph and coldstart kb view each produce a single self-contained HTML file from a template carrying a <!--__HOME_LINK__--> placeholder; the CLI's own render call (renderGraphHtml / renderViewHtml) unconditionally clears that placeholder to '' because the standalone local file has nowhere to link back to, so the website build scripts (the only callers that want the link) must substitute the real <a id="home"> anchor into the raw template BEFORE calling render — filling it in after render is a silent no-op.

steps.role: defines the placeholder + #home CSS, original pattern
substitutes the real home link into the template before calling renderGraphHtml
gained the same placeholder + #home CSS this session, mirroring the graph template
now also clears the placeholder for the standalone CLI case
new generator script — substitutes the real home link before calling renderViewHtml

invariants: the placeholder must be filled on the TEMPLATE string before calling render() — render always clears it, so filling it in after is a no-op that silently ships a link-less page
both viewers use the identical anchor markup/id (#home) and CSS convention — a future third generated viewer should follow the same order
